advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether DC transition resolution should be case/whitespace-insensitive like the Cloud sibling, or document why exact-match is intentional for DC.
evidence: transport.py:300: `match = next((t for t in entries if t.get("name") == target_status), None)`
transport.py:306: `if isinstance(t.get("to"), dict) and t["to"].get("name") == target_status`

Sibling Cloud impl normalizes: acli.py:519-521 `name = (t.get("name") or "").strip().lower()` / `to_name = ((t.get("to") or {}).get("name") or "").strip().lower()` / `if target_lower in (name, to_name)`
The epic's stated theme (per docstring/ticket) is that DC-shaped instances diverge from Cloud conventions, so a casing mismatch is exactly the class of surprise to expect on a real DC workflow.
transport.py:306: fallback depends on `t["to"].get("name")` being populated

ABSENCE: `jira`/`jira.JIRA.transitions` is not installed in this environment (resolve_symbol UNRESOLVED), so the default presence of `to` in the pycontribs transitions() response could not be confirmed here; unit tests only exercise a fake that always supplies `to`.
The ticket AC covers this via the DC harness (test_outbound_mutation_round_trips[04-transition-status]), which is the real safeguard — but the unit suite alone cannot catch a missing-`to` regression.
advisory.finding: The DC resolver matches transition name and to.name with exact equality (t.get("name") == target_status), while the sibling Cloud implementation normalizes case/whitespace (.strip().lower()) before comparing. Casing or whitespace drift between LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA values and the DC server's status/transition strings would miss and re-trigger the same silent-partial-failure class this fix exists to close.
merged_from: The destination-status fallback assumes the client's transitions() payload includes each entry's to.name, but the production call passes no expand argument; if a real DC server omits 'to' from the default transitions response the fallback never matches and the fix silently no-ops in production while passing on the fake.
scenarios: A DC workflow whose status is 'In progress' (or with trailing whitespace) while LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA holds 'In Progress' — the lookup misses and the change silently soft-fails again.

coaching.coaching: File a follow-on ticket (discovered_from this change) for case/whitespace normalization parity with the Cloud resolver, a pre-existing / out-of-scope issue — do not fix it in this change.
coaching.subject: case/whitespace normalization parity with the Cloud resolver
